The $BTC Death Spiral 🧵 (or the ultimate bottom tweet)

1. Macro turns. Sticky inflation, high rates, strong dollar. BTC still trades like levered Nasdaq.

2. AI eats liquidity. Speculative money chases AI stocks. No new BTC buyers.

3. Chart breaks. Monthly close under $58k confirms lower highs from $126k. Trend funds exit.

4. Leverage flush. Cascading liquidations punch through support.

5. ETF outflows. Underwater holders redeem. The biggest bid since 2024 flips to selling.

6. OG holders sell. Dormant coins moving adds fear.

7. Quantum FUD. ~1.7M+ BTC with exposed keys, Satoshi's included, look stealable. Freeze vs. migrate fight splits the community.

8. Treasury cos crack. $MSTR and copycats trade below NAV. Issuing shares stops working. Converts and preferreds come due. Forced BTC sales.

9. Contagion. A forced seller or stablecoin wobble. 2022 all over again.

10. Miners capitulate. 2028 halving cuts the reward to 1.5625 BTC into a falling price. Reserves dumped, power flipped to AI data centers.

11. Fees don't fill the gap. Weak on-chain activity. Fees are a rounding error. Hashrate falls.

12. Security budget crisis. Cheaper 51% attacks go mainstream. "Digital gold" cracks.

13. Rivals take share. Tokenized gold, stablecoins, CBDCs, self-custody crackdowns.

14. Reflexive loop. Lower price, more forced selling, less security, more fear.

tweets.text:
Three weeks after Euro Pacific Bank was placed into receivership, an independent group of experienced banking professionals—including a former OCIF commissioner—approached OCIF about buying the bank.

They wanted to replace management and the board with more experienced people, fully recapitalize the bank, and cure the deficiencies OCIF cited to justify its closure. The goal was to meet regulatory requirements, protect customers, reopen the bank, and restore their access to their deposits.

Yet OCIF Commissioner Natalia I. Zequeira Díaz refused to even consider this potential rescue.

The reason is clear. Rescuing the bank conflicted with the publicity objectives of the IRS, its J5 partners, and OCIF itself. They needed a shutdown they could portray as a victory against tax evasion and money laundering. Selling and recapitalizing the bank would have undermined their effort to make an innocent bank look guilty.

The failure to allow a sale that would have fully cured all of the official deficiencies cited to justify receivership proves that those deficiencies were just a pretext. The J5 publicity stunt required the bank to be shut down, so the OCIF commissioner needed to fabricate a reason to justify it.

So Commissioner Zequeira Díaz sacrificed the interests of customers to serve a publicity campaign. The very legislative purpose of OCIF is to protect customers. Yet because of OCIF, it's now been more than four years, and only a handful of depositors have been repaid. From what I can tell, most will never get their money back.

Yet every single depositor would have been made whole had OCIF done the right thing and approved the sale, which also would have provided me with millions of dollars as the seller. Yet because the OCIF commissioner cared more about helping the J5 frame the bank than saving its customers, she rejected the sale.

So the very government entity created to protect bank customers is the reason so many have lost their deposits. This is why no one outside of Puerto Rico should bank in Puerto Rico. 

You can read the contemporaneous email from my lawyer here: https://9fraud.com/potential-buyer-interest-in-euro-pacific-bank/
